correctness.rationale: Final file: /workspace/repairs/2/RESULT.md. The frozen prior-work sentence said equality with factor complexity held precisely at powers of two, but its own length-three base case gives b_2(3)=5=P(3). The corrected paragraph credits dyadic equality and finite computations without that false exclusivity. The theorem and scope are unchanged and checked on the corrected file. At fixed length all counts through order two follow from (z,t). By p_(2j)=0 and p_(2j+1)=1−p_j, every factor of doubled length is an even or odd lift of a shorter factor and both lifts occur for each shorter factor. Complementing swaps 01 with 10; the inserted zeros give T_B=binom(z,2)+2[z(m−z)−t] and T_A=T_B+z. There are no adjacent ones, and all five length-three words with no adjacent ones occur in the opening prefix; their signatures give the three claimed base tiers. The injective t maps in an odd tier have opposite parity, so outer sizes double. In the even middle tier the new step is z and the two images differ by one step, growing the progression by one term. This proves all k≥0 for the full factor language. An independent direct test generated the first 32768 letters from the parity recurrence and counted signatures for starts 0 through 32768−3·2^k, checking k=0 through 8. It reproduced 5,8,13,22,39,72,137,266,523 and the tier data. That finite test is corroboration, not a completeness argument about arbitrary starts. The supplied verifier was inspected, not run.

value.rationale: The length-three dyadic ray is the first non-power-of-two core and a natural uniform-substitution family. Known dyadic separation leaves genuine signature collisions unresolved outside it. The exact additive k term and disjointness-versus-overlap mechanism describe how the classes change under doubling; the result supplies more than numerical first values. The literature clarification preserves this content and its significance without overstating dyadic exclusivity.
